advances:
This replaces the separate Brunn--Minkowski estimates for the two large
midpoint bodies by one affine-invariant mixed-area gate inside the common
plane.  It also gives the exact weighted \(R^\star\)-charge of their joint
hull.  Either of two explicit strict inequalities then excludes the
single-double branch: one forces \(k\ge M+m\), while the other contradicts
the common-level ledger \(W^\star=0\).  The gate is not tied to the
symmetric calibration.  It is stated in four normalized invariants and
therefore covers an explicit open neighborhood.  Applied to accepted fact
`70ae511e2c57d140`, it shows that the first two bodies already force
\(k>M+m\); the third body is unnecessary for that family.  Applied to the
large-\(p/M\), large-\(k/M\) scalar escape, it gives an exact missing
mixed-area threshold and verifies that the scalar table itself lies
outside both gates.  Thus the result does not promote the scalar
relaxation to a geometric contradiction; it isolates the remaining
common-plane task.

proof:
All closures introduced above change exact cells only on finitely many
cutting lines, which have planar area zero by accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f`.  The cells are bounded and convex, so their closures
are compact and convex.  A finite convex hull commutes with taking these
closures, and the boundary of a planar convex body has area zero.  This
proves the assertion relating the closed and exact hulls.

For arbitrary convex sets \(P,Q_1,Q_2\),
\[
\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P+Q_1)\cup(P+Q_2)\bigr)
=P+\operatorname{conv}(Q_1\cup Q_2).
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, a convex combination of \(p_1+q_1\) and \(p_2+q_2\) equals
\[
\bigl((1-\lambda)p_1+\lambda p_2\bigr)
+\bigl((1-\lambda)q_1+\lambda q_2\bigr)
\]
and belongs to the right-hand side.  Conversely,
\[
p+(1-\lambda)q_1+\lambda q_2
=(1-\lambda)(p+q_1)+\lambda(p+q_2)
\]
belongs to the left-hand side.  Scaling (14) by \(1/2\) gives the first
identity in (2).  Formula (1), followed by area scaling by \(1/4\),
gives the area identity in (2).  Since \(H_{12}\subseteq H\subseteq K\),
the remaining inequalities in (2) and implication (4) follow.

The singleton incidences in accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` put
\(B_1\) in \(R_1\) and \(B_2\) in \(R_2\), up to null cutting-line
boundaries.  Also, for \(x\in P\) and
\(y\in\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2}\),
\[
2f_3\!\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)
=\bigl(f_3(x)-L_3\bigr)+\bigl(f_3(y)+L_3\bigr)\ge0.
\]
Convexity therefore puts all of \(H_{12}\), modulo null boundaries, in
\(R_1\cup R_2\cup R_{12}\).  The \(R^\star\)-coefficients on these
three cells are \(3/2,3/2,5\).  Hence the exact charge carried by
\(H_{12}\) is
\[
\frac32\bigl(|H_{12}|-\Gamma\bigr)+5\Gamma
=\frac32|H_{12}|+\frac72\Gamma.
\tag{15}
\]
Every \(R^\star\)-coefficient is nonnegative.  Since
\(H_{12}\subseteq K\), (15) proves (3).

Accepted fact `1e269d4c02c94338` gives the exact common-level
decomposition
\[
W^\star=-2p+\mathcal P^\star+\mathcal Q^\star+\mathcal R^\star_K.
\tag{16}
\]
The three crossings give \(W^\star=W\), and \(W=0\) is assumed.
Combining (3) and (16) proves implication (5).

Under a nonsingular affine map, \(p,\sigma,V(P,C),M,m,\Gamma\), and all
cell areas are multiplied by the same absolute determinant.  Thus
(4)--(8) and the normalized quantities are affine invariant.  Dividing
(4) and (5) by \(M>0\) gives (6) and (7), while the stated lower and
upper bounds in (8) imply (6).

It remains to audit the claimed neighborhood of the accepted family.
The source-cell polygons listed in accepted fact
`70ae511e2c57d140` show that
\(C=\operatorname{conv}(\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2})\) is the
trapezoid with vertices
\[
(-2(D+2),-D-4),\quad(2(D+2),-D-4),
\]
\[
(-(D+2),-D-2),\quad(D+2,-D-2).
\]
Its area is \(6(D+2)\), proving the first formula in (9).

Pruning only the vertices of
\(\operatorname{conv}(\overline{B_1}\cup\overline{B_2})\) from the
same accepted lists gives the symmetric octagon with vertex pairs
\[
\left(\pm\frac{5D+7}{4},-\frac{D+9}{4}\right),\qquad
\left(\pm\frac{5D+9}{4},-\frac{D+7}{4}\right),
\]
\[
\left(\pm\frac{2D+5}{2},-2\right),\qquad
\left(\pm\frac{D+3}{2},-1\right).
\]
The shoelace formula gives (10).  In this family
\[
p_D=\frac{D^2+6D-3}{4}.
\]
Substituting this value, \(\sigma_D=6D+12\), and (10) into the mixed
area identity (2) yields
\[
V_D=D^2+3D+4,
\]
which completes (9).  Subtracting
\[
M_D+m_D=\frac{D^2+38D+73}{4}
\]
from (10) gives (11).  Its numerator is positive at \(D=28\) and has
positive derivative for \(D\ge28\).

The left side of (12) equals
\[
\frac{4(|H_{12}|-M_D-m_D)}{M_D}
=\frac{5D^2-98D-215}{(D+3)^2}.
\]
Subtracting \(1\) gives
\[
\frac{4(D^2-26D-56)}{(D+3)^2}\ge0
\qquad(D\ge28),
\]
with equality at \(D=28\).  The triangle inequality now shows that
(13) changes the left side of (12) by less than \(1\), so the perturbed
geometry satisfies (6) strictly.

Finally, test the gates against the scalar escape rather than treating
that table as common-plane data.  Its values are
\[
M=k=10000,\quad m=1,\quad
p=\frac{199997}{20},\quad q_1=q_2=\frac25.
\]
Any actual \(C\) contains the disjoint positive-area cells \(Q_1,Q_2\)
and is contained in \(A_2\), so
\[
\frac45\le\sigma\le1.
\tag{17}
\]
Because \(H_{12}\subseteq K\), (2) and the left inequality in (17)
force
\[
V(P,C)
\le 20000-\frac{p+\sigma}{2}
\le\frac{599987}{40}.
\tag{18}
\]
In contrast, the easiest possible area gate, using the right inequality
in (17), would require
\[
V(P,C)
\ge 20002-\frac{p+\sigma}{2}
\ge\frac{600063}{40}.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus the scalar escape cannot pass the mixed-area gate merely by
choosing its free common-plane geometry.

For the charge gate, its endpoint contribution is
\[
\mathcal P^\star+\mathcal Q^\star=\frac{51}{20},
\]
and its scalar bridge capacity is
\(\Gamma\le r_{12}=1/20000\).  Again using
\(|H_{12}|\le k=10000\), the left side of (5) is at most
\[
15000+\frac7{40000},
\]
whereas its right side is
\[
2p-\mathcal P^\star-\mathcal Q^\star
=\frac{399943}{20}.
\]
Hence the scalar table also lies outside the charge gate.  This is the
precise surviving boundary: a proof against that escape must either
derive the missing lower bound (19) from the three actual crossings, or
extract additional charged section area created by \(B_3\).  Neither
conclusion follows from the scalar table alone.
statement:
Assume the affine-plane and exact-cell setting of accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f`, relabeled so that the positive \(Q\)-support is
\(\{123,1,2,12\}\).  Assume also the three crossing equalities and
\(W=0\) used in accepted fact `1e269d4c02c94338`.  Put
\[
P=\overline{P_\varnothing},\qquad
C=\operatorname{conv}(\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2}),
\qquad p=|P|,\qquad \sigma=|C|.
\]
Let \(V(P,C)\) denote planar mixed area in the normalization
\[
|P+C|=p+\sigma+2V(P,C).
\tag{1}
\]
Define
\[
B_1=\frac{P+\overline{Q_1}}2,\qquad
B_2=\frac{P+\overline{Q_2}}2,\qquad
B_3=\frac{\overline{P_3}+\overline{Q_{123}}}2,
\]
\[
H_{12}=\operatorname{conv}(B_1\cup B_2),\qquad
H=\operatorname{conv}(B_1\cup B_2\cup B_3),
\]
and
\[
\Gamma=\left|H_{12}\cap R_{12}\right|.
\]
The closed hull \(H\) is the closure of the hull formed with the exact
half-open cells, so the two hulls have the same planar area.

Then
\[
H_{12}=\frac{P+C}{2},
\qquad
|H|\ge |H_{12}|
=\frac{p+\sigma+2V(P,C)}4.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, if
\[
\mathcal R^\star_K
=\frac32(r_1+r_2)+5r_{12}
+\frac72(r_{13}+r_{23})+7r_{123},
\]
then
\[
\mathcal R^\star_K
\ge
\frac32|H_{12}|+\frac72\Gamma
=\frac38\bigl(p+\sigma+2V(P,C)\bigr)+\frac72\Gamma.
\tag{3}
\]

Write
\[
\mathcal P^\star
=\frac32(p_1+p_2)+5p_{12}
+\frac72(p_{13}+p_{23}),
\]
\[
\mathcal Q^\star
=\frac32(q_1+q_2)+5q_{12}+7q_{123}.
\]
Consequently either one of the following two gates excludes the branch:
\[
p+\sigma+2V(P,C)\ge4(M+m)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
k\ge M+m,
\tag{4}
\]
\[
\frac38\bigl(p+\sigma+2V(P,C)\bigr)+\frac72\Gamma
>
2p-\mathcal P^\star-\mathcal Q^\star
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
W^\star>0,
\tag{5}
\]
where the three crossings give \(W^\star=W=0\), so (5) is impossible.

Both gates are affine invariant.  More explicitly, put
\[
\pi=\frac pM,\qquad
\mu=\frac mM,\qquad
\chi=\frac{\sigma}{M},\qquad
\nu=\frac{V(P,C)}M,\qquad
\gamma=\frac{\Gamma}{M},\qquad
\rho=\frac{\mathcal P^\star+\mathcal Q^\star}{M}.
\]
Then (4) and (5) become, respectively,
\[
\pi+\chi+2\nu\ge4(1+\mu),
\tag{6}
\]
\[
\frac38(\pi+\chi+2\nu)+\frac72\gamma
>2\pi-\rho.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus, for example, whenever \(p/M\ge1-\varepsilon\),
\(m/M\le\mu_0\), \(\sigma/M\ge\chi_0\), and
\(V(P,C)/M\ge\nu_0\), the explicit condition
\[
1-\varepsilon+\chi_0+2\nu_0\ge4(1+\mu_0)
\tag{8}
\]
forces \(k/M\ge1+m/M\).  In particular it excludes a scalar escape
with \(k/M<1+m/M\), including one with both \(p/M\) and \(k/M\) near
\(1\).

For the family in accepted fact `70ae511e2c57d140`,
\[
\sigma_D=6D+12,\qquad
V_D=D^2+3D+4,
\tag{9}
\]
and
\[
|H_{12}|=\frac{9D^2+54D+77}{16}.
\tag{10}
\]
Hence
\[
|H_{12}|-(M_D+m_D)
=\frac{5D^2-98D-215}{16}>0
\qquad(D\ge28).
\tag{11}
\]
This conclusion holds on a quantitative neighborhood, not only on the
displayed triangles.  If
\[
\pi_D=\frac{p_D}{M_D},\quad
\mu_D=\frac{m_D}{M_D},\quad
\chi_D=\frac{\sigma_D}{M_D},\quad
\nu_D=\frac{V_D}{M_D},
\]
then
\[
\pi_D+\chi_D+2\nu_D-4(1+\mu_D)
=\frac{5D^2-98D-215}{(D+3)^2}\ge1.
\tag{12}
\]
Therefore every actual single-double geometry satisfying
\[
|\pi-\pi_D|+|\chi-\chi_D|
+2|\nu-\nu_D|+4|\mu-\mu_D|<1
\tag{13}
\]
satisfies the strict area gate (6).
